news.title: Lionel Messi returns after World Cup heartbreak in Miami draw
news.lede: Lionel Messi made his long-awaited return to competitive football after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain, but Inter Miami were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw against the Columbus Crew in Major League Soccer.The Argentine captain came off the bench in the 53rd minute, marking his first appearance since the World Cup final. Fellow Argentina international Rodrigo De Paul also returned to action, starting in midfield for Miami.Messi was unable to make an immediate impact on the scoresheet, although he went close twice in the second half. His best chance came deep into stoppage time, but his effort drifted wide as Miami failed to snatch a late winner.. The match had kicked off 40 minutes late due to a weather delay.Instead, Luis Suarez continued his rich vein of form.

news.title: Infantino under pressure as Uefa demands accountability over failed World Cup plan
news.lede: Uefa has declared it has no confidence in Fifa President Gianni Infantino after he abandoned a controversial plan to sell a stake in World Cup profits to private investors, deepening a leadership crisis in world football. The proposal sought to place Fifa's commercial operations, including the men's and women's World Cups, into a $20 billion company with 20% owned by private investors. The plan collapsed yesterday (2 August) following strong opposition from Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), CONCACAF and an internal revolt within Fifa. Aleksander Čeferin, Uefa President, said the current Fifa leadership had lost the confidence of Europe and many others in global football, insisting those responsible for the proposal must be held accountable.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: Zinedine Zidane Begins a New Era as France Coach After 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Zinedine Zidane has waited years for the opportunity he describes as the biggest challenge in football. On Tuesday, 28 July, the French Football Federation appointed the former World Cup winner as head coach of France on a contract running through the 2030 FIFA World Cup, completing a succession plan that had been anticipated for several seasons. Zidane replaces Didier Deschamps after France’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended with a semifinal defeat to Spain and a 6-4 loss to England in the third-place match. His first assignment comes quickly, with UEFA Nations League away fixtures against Turkey on Sept. 25 and Belgium three days later before France hosts Italy and Belgium in early October.

news.title: 'Nobody is selling football!' - FIFA responds to controversy and offers explanation after Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan sparks outrage
news.lede: FIFA has issued a firm response to the mounting backlash surrounding its controversial World Cup spin-off proposal, insisting that "nobody is selling football." The governing body claims media reports mischaracterised the plans and reaffirmed its commitment to a democratic process. FIFA has officially responded to the fierce opposition surrounding its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project. The governing body released a public statement attempting to clear up what it described as "incorrect media reports" that disrupted the planned consultation process.

news.title: Gianni Infantino ‘has lost Uefa’s confidence’ after Fifa chief scraps World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: Infantino ditched proposals after widespread backlash. Uefa adds: ‘We cannot keep going on with secret schemes’. Uefa has warned Gianni Infantino that his style of leadership cannot continue in demanding a thorough and fundamental review of Fifa’s governance. In a strongly worded statement that referred to “secret schemes”, “shabby backroom deals” and “faceless individuals”, the Uefa leadership made clear it wants change at the top of Fifa, despite the world governing body’s overnight U-turn in abandoning Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.

news.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was elected Fifa president in 2016. A week is a long time in politics. On Tuesday morning, Gianni Infantino was in an impregnable position as Fifa president, the most powerful job in football. Now, after trying to sell stakes in Fifa competitions to private investments firms - apparently without the knowledge of anyone else - Infantino's position appears to be under threat.

news.title: FIFA faces fresh transparency calls after retreat on World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: FIFA faced renewed calls for transparency on Saturday after it abruptly shelved plans to sell a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup, a proposal that triggered fierce ‌backlash from regional confederations that said they had been blindsided. The swift reversal has exposed growing unease within world soccer over FIFA President Gianni Infantino's leadership style, with football officials demanding greater oversight of decisions that could reshape the governance and commercial future ‌of the sport. The backlash has also raised questions about Infantino's political capital as ⁠he prepares to seek another term in office. FIFA's plan was to raise up to $4.2 ⁠billion by selling about ⁠a 20% stake to private investors in a new unit that would run FIFA events, including the ‌World Cup.
